title: position with a CSS-wide keyword (unset/initial/inherit/revert) is emitted before an earlier position value
impact: Silently inverts the cascade for `position: absolute; position: unset` in one block, including after merging two adjacent same-selector rules (reporter says a Vite upgrade triggered the merge in production). No reactions; filed in a same-day batch of spec-precise reports. Same handler also mis-orders direction and unicode-bidi. Present since at least 1.14.0.
code: src/properties/position.rs: PositionHandler::handle_property (no Property::Unparsed arm, so the unparsed decl is pushed immediately while the parsed one is buffered until finalize)
src/declaration.rs: DeclarationHandler::handle_all (direction/unicode-bidi buffered as Option, same pattern)
src/properties/mod.rs: Property::parse (values that fail the typed parser, including CSS-wide keywords, become Property::Unparsed)
summary: CSS-wide keywords on `position` are not parsed into the typed Position value; Property::parse falls back to Property::Unparsed, exactly like `position: var(--x)`. PositionHandler ignores Unparsed, so it is emitted immediately while the earlier parsed `position` is emitted at finalize, after it. This is the same root cause as #1225 (var()), just a different way to reach Property::Unparsed.
repro: triage/sweep/1391-repro.mjs. `.x{position:absolute;position:unset}` -> `.x{position:unset;position:absolute}` on master, 1.33.0, 1.32.0, 1.31.1 (every release back to 1.14.0). Also initial/inherit/revert/revert-layer, non-minified output, merged adjacent rules, sticky with safari 12 prefixes, and `direction:rtl;direction:unset` / `unicode-bidi:isolate;unicode-bidi:initial`. Controls `position:unset;position:absolute` and `display:flex;display:inherit` are correct.
evidence: repro.mjs on local master + 1.33.0/1.32.0/1.31.1, --range 1.0.0..1.33.0 (wrong in all 1.14.0..1.33.0). equivalence.mjs --quick on `.x{position:absolute;top:1px}.x{position:unset}` with --minify: NOT EQUIVALENT, computed position static -> absolute. Code read: CSS-wide keyword values go through the Unparsed fallback in Property::parse.

fix.approach: Handle Property::Unparsed{property_id: Position} in PositionHandler by flushing then pushing (as other handlers and the shorthand_handler! macro do); same for direction/unicode-bidi in handle_all. PR #1387 does exactly this.

openPRs.assessment: Fixes the root cause for #1225 and therefore this issue too: it matches any Property::Unparsed with PropertyId::Position (CSS-wide keywords included) and keeps direction/unicode-bidi in source order. Tests only cover var(); suggest adding `position:absolute;position:unset` and a merged-rules case. Not built.

draftReply:
Thanks for the clear report! This has the same cause as #1225: when a `position` value isn't a plain keyword like `absolute` (that includes `unset`/`initial`/`inherit`/`revert` as well as `var()`), Lightning CSS keeps it as raw tokens, and the `position` handler emits it right away while holding back the earlier value until the end of the block. That's why `.x{position:absolute;position:unset}` becomes `.x{position:unset;position:absolute}`. `direction` and `unicode-bidi` behave the same way.

There's an open PR, #1387, that addresses #1225 and should cover this case as well. Until then, `position: static` works as you found. Closing in favour of #1225 so the discussion stays in one place.
